architecture.decision: Each person's agentmux hub stays the local owner of its own data: one hub process per machine owns an SQLite hub.db and the local socket protocol (docs/PROTOCOL.md). Cross-user collaboration is a separate, opt-in layer (hub/fed/) in which hubs connect as plain NATS clients, not leaf nodes, to one hosted JetStream cluster (deploy/nats, Helm chart nats 2.15.0) with operator/account/user JWTs. Messages, work, board, knowledge and code are delivered through a transactional outbox and an idempotent inbox, one plugin per capability behind one guard pipeline. The dashboard is a local operator console served by dashboard/server.py on 127.0.0.1 and is scoped as part of the backend surface, not as a separate web application.
architecture.rationale: Agents keep the local hub protocol and work offline; crossing to another person must not change how an agent posts or claims. The NATS server enforces sender identity (per-user publish ACLs on subject token 3), and per-peer trust plus per-repo opt-in keep data local by default (docs/FEDERATION.md sections 3, 4, 6 and 8).
alternatives: A leaf node per machine: rejected, because JetStream plus the local outbox already give offline buffering and a leaf node adds a server per machine (docs/FEDERATION.md A8).
One shared broker for every hub with no local store: rejected, because it removes local offline operation and per-person trust (.context/design-patterns.md FED-01).
Publishing directly from the verb without an outbox: rejected, because it loses messages on disconnect (.context/design-patterns.md FED-02).
Core NATS plus local outboxes only, without JetStream: rejected, because nothing survives the receiver being offline (.context/design-patterns.md FED-03).
constraints: The core hub stays stdlib-only; nats-py and its transitives live only in .venv, pinned by hub/requirements.lock (docs/FEDERATION.md A4).
The circle (one NATS account) is the confidentiality boundary; per-repo peers limit only sending and mirroring (docs/FEDERATION.md A7, 7.4).
Subject tokens are [a-z0-9_] and the sender is taken from subject token 3 only, never from the payload (docs/FEDERATION.md 4-5, docs/PROTOCOL.md 11).
Remote work never triggers privileged tools without operator approval (docs/FEDERATION.md F11, 7.2).
One circle per hub in v1 (docs/FEDERATION.md A5). The harness runs on macOS and WSL from one checkout and needs tmux 3.x and bash 5.

build: python3 -m py_compile hub/*.py hub/fed/*.py hub/fed/plugins/*.py hub/fed/hooks/*.py
